title: Matignon's Cipher-3, 1586: two Poitou intelligence notes (BnF fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) and a six-page despatch to the King (fr. 15573 ff. 379-381)

steps.what: Located the two Cipher-3 leaves on the images: fr. 15571 f. 179 at canvas 187 left (bound upside down; first listed as 'f. 178v, fourth hand') and fr. 15572 f. 276 at canvas 285 right; siblings ff. 277r-278r deciphered in ff. 279-280.

alejandrozarco (PR #25): Tomokiyo's partial Cipher-3 table checked by hard-EM alignment of a blind transcription of sibling f. 277r against its contemporary decipherment on ff. 279-280; values added (### = et, two-stroke # = i, dotted v = u, S-shape = q and others).
alejandrozarco (PR #25): f. 276 (22 lines) and fr. 15571 f. 179 (21 lines) transcribed sign by sign twice, independently; reads agree on 93.8% (f. 276) and 91.5% (f. 179) of signs.

alejandrozarco (PR #25): f. 276 deciphered with the Cipher-3 key, 698/734 signs (95.1%) in lexical runs (fr-henri4 word list); f. 179 transcribed and checked against Tomokiyo's unpublished magenta interlinear decipherment, 466/509 (91.6%). Poitou faction report naming La Rousiere, la Mare, Iehan Durant, Lansac.

Review of PR #25: measure.py re-run reproduces 698/734 and 466/509; 50 shuffled keys give median 6.3% / 3.1% (max 21.5% / 21.0%); line structure of f. 276 L01, L21, L22 and f. 179 L18 (blot), L21 checked on the Gallica natives.

alejandrozarco, after the PR #25 review: measure.py and control_shuffle.py now take their lexicon from the shared lang/ model fr-1600-letters (corpora.text + lm.norm 'early', words >= 20 occurrences) instead of bundled word lists, which are removed. f. 276 706/734 (96.2%; 50 shuffled keys median 6.9%), f. 179 473/509 (92.9%; median 3.5%); the difference from the word list is mainly 'veullent' reaching 20 occurrences under lang normalisation. f. 276 L18 read as 'redoute la [K]; quelque chose', making the C-with-epsilon sign q and K a one-sign code word (paix? Ligue? Royne?).

Split from the former combined target matignon1586 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the two Cipher-3 leaves are their own entry; f276/ and f179/ moved here. measure.py re-run on both read_final.txt files reproduces 706/734 and 473/509.

Contributed (Brett Burford, issue #44, v0.1-v0.5 18-19 Oct 2026): fr. 15573 ff. 379r-381v, 2,836 signs read by Claude Opus 5.5 under a sign sheet, five passes voted, corrections decided on the image; Tomokiyo's Cipher-3 key checked on ff. 277-280 and extended from the 1585 letter fr. 15570 ff. 271-273; two-valued signs chosen by whole words. His measure: 0.90-0.95 of signs per page in French words, shuffled 0.59-0.78; 5 short runs and 5 rare code signs open.

Re-measured here with this entry's rule (f276/scripts/measure.py, fr-1600-letters, 20 shuffled keys) on his signs through his recorded key choices (f379_381/to_read.py): f. 379r 440/503, 379v 447/490, 380r 420/492, 380v 493/532, 381r 479/524, 381v 261/295 = 2,540/2,836 (89.6%); shuffled medians 5.8-9.8%, max 33%. View 740 compared with his f. 379r signs: 22 cipher lines as he has them, and the opening signs of l. 2 (b, a, a hooked sign, 30) correspond.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): alejandrozarco's sign-by-sign reads and reconciled readings for f. 276 and f. 179 (with SOLUTION.md), Brett Burford's per-page signs, plaintext, French text and English gist for fr. 15573 ff. 379-381 plus read_all.txt; keys key-cipher3.json, key_em_all.tsv and the Key section of f276/SOLUTION.md.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): f. 276 and f. 179 read from SOLUTION.md (A); fr. 15573 ff. 379-381 (Burford v0.5) has a garbled word in nearly every sentence and no translation (C confirmed). Relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part kept; fraction_read 0.9118 -> 0.305.

fr. 15573 ff. 379-381: Gallica btv1b90618780 views 740-745 fetched at full size (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF); f. 379r ll. 1-3 compared with Burford's sign names (no label changed). No contemporary decipherment, print or DECODE record; no other copy of the Cipher-3 key found.

fr. 15573 ff. 379-381: Burford's literal decode divided and punctuated into a partial reading with every departure bracketed (54 [?word]s; new: 'veu la saison qui est proche de l'iuer', 'president [?Brulart]', 'baillant trois cents escus a vostre seur'), English added. b17_score.py (fr): 0.299 (20/67), explicit holes 0.433; Burford's unpunctuated normalised text scores 0.55 only because code word-breaks cut garble into short words. Kept decoded, not read.

fr. 15573 views 724-757 (ff. 368-387) contact-sheeted and ff. 377-378 read at 1400 px for a clear copy, minute or decipherment of ff. 379-381: none (ff. 377-378 are town petitions to the King; ff. 382-384 blank and address; ff. 385-386 another cipher addressed to Villeroy).

research/reading_audit/r2j_lattice.py: word lattice over Burford's signs with the Henri IV letters' vocabulary, single-sign substitutions tallied per sign class. Recurring second values kept after a word-by-word check: C = h, p+ = b, b = y, g = o, Lr = n; rejected d = s, z3 = et, 9t = e (value).

ff. 379-381 re-read at every break on the full-size IIIF views (four-line bands): f. 379v l. 3 bleed-through p removed ('la dite riuiere'); reading rebuilt with the second values and look-alike alternates (28 letters, 1.2%); unbracketed words checked against the signs with r2j_matignon_carry.py and b30's unsupported words corrected. v2_score fr: explicit holes 0.344 -> 0.590 (36/61), plain 0.279 -> 0.426. Marked read (B), at the edge of the bar.

texts.label: fr. 15572 f. 276, 1586 (alejandrozarco, PR #25)
texts.summary: A Poitou intelligence note on the Catholic factions round La Roussière, Henri III's governor of Fontenay(-le-Comte): La Guiolle unsure of Le Puy, La Saussaie, the priory promised to Aubois, the sieurs de la Fontaine, la Chaie and Mirebeau; 'Le Pui est ennuyé de la guerre'. Writer and recipient are not named. The transcriptions are the two independent sign-by-sign reads (one letter per sign).

texts.label: fr. 15571 f. 179, 1586 (alejandrozarco, PR #25)
texts.summary: Frontin is to come to terms with La Rousière's children; the writer is resolved to attack Pons, 'il se poura prendre en ung mois'; sickness among the foot; 'employer Lansac en ... l'armée de mer'. The siege and the sickness fit, without being established, the plague in Mayenne's and Matignon's army round Castillon (Aug-Sept 1586); Tomokiyo's interlinear decipherment was the check.

texts.label: fr. 15573 ff. 379r-381v, autumn 1586 (Brett Burford, issue #44)
texts.summary: A six-page despatch wholly in cipher, addressed to the King and probably from Matignon: a military report on the Guyenne campaign, the river trade on the Garonne between Toulouse and Bordeaux from which the Huguenots draw dues, Caumont and the Mas de Verdun, Castillon, the Isle and the Dordogne, the King of Navarre, 'your sister' at Agen, the artillery from Navarrenx, Marmande and fifteen to sixteen thousand crowns. Read by Brett Burford (v0.5, 19 Oct 2026); his files are copied with his licence.
